title: Azure Regions, Zones and Datacenters

header.html: Describe Azure regions, region pairs, and sovereign regions; Describe availability zones; Describe Azure datacenters
the official AZ-900 study guide, skills measured as of July 20, 2026

html:
1The physical layers of Azure

Azure runs on a worldwide network of datacenters. They are grouped into regions, and some regions are split into availability zones.

Layer What it is
Datacenter A physical building with servers, power, cooling and network
Availability zone A physically separate group of one or more datacenters inside one region, with independent power, cooling and networking
Region A set of datacenters deployed within a latency-defined perimeter and connected by a dedicated low-latency network
Region pair Two regions in the same geography, set up to protect each other
Geography A market area (often a country or group of countries) that keeps data and compliance boundaries

2Regions

A region is where you choose to deploy a resource, for example East US or West Europe. Most resources are tied to one region, so you pick the region when you create them.

Choose a region by:

  • Location near users (lower latency).
  • Data residency and compliance needs (keep data in a country or area).
  • Service availability: not every service or size is in every region.
  • Price: the same service can cost different amounts in different regions.
Exam tip

. Resource location is a property of the resource. A resource group has its own location (where metadata is stored), but its resources can be in other regions.

3Region pairs

Most regions are paired with another region in the same geography, usually hundreds of miles apart. [Verify live] Many newer regions have availability zones and no region pair.

Benefits of a pair:

  • Recovery priority: if there is a broad outage, one region of each pair is recovered first.
  • Planned updates: Azure strives to stagger planned system updates across the regions of a pair, so both are not updated together.
  • Data residency: pairs stay in the same geography (with exceptions) so data stays in the area.
  • Some services use the pair for geo-redundant replication (for example geo-redundant storage, Module 8).

4Sovereign regions

Sovereign regions are instances of Azure that are isolated from the main (public) Azure instance, to meet special legal or compliance needs.

Sovereign region For
Azure Government US government agencies and their partners
Microsoft Azure operated by 21Vianet (Azure China) Customers in China, run by a local partner
Exam tip

. If a question mentions government compliance or operating in China with a local operator, think sovereign regions. They are physically and logically separate from the global Azure regions.

5Availability zones

An availability zone (AZ) is a physically separate location inside a region. Each zone has independent power, cooling and networking. Regions that support zones have at least three of them. [Verify live]

Use zones to protect against a failure of a single datacenter:

Option Meaning Examples
Zonal services You choose the zone where the resource runs a virtual machine placed in zone 1
Zone-redundant services Azure replicates the resource across zones for you zone-redundant storage, zone-redundant databases
Non-regional (always available) services Not tied to one region; resilient to zone and region failure Microsoft Entra ID (Module 9)
Exam tip

. Zones protect inside a region (datacenter failure). Region pairs protect across regions (regional disaster). Not every region has zones.

Availability sets Beyond the study guide: appears under VM options in Module 6 spread VMs across fault and update domains inside one datacenter, a weaker option than zones.

6Azure datacenters

Azure datacenters are large, secured facilities with:

  • Physical security: controlled access, monitoring.
  • Redundant power and cooling and many network connections.
  • A Microsoft global network that links the datacenters.

Microsoft maintains the datacenters, hardware and physical network. You choose where your resources run (region and zone), not which building.

7Exam Q&A

7.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Fabrikam Outdoors wants its app to keep running if one datacenter in the region fails. Which feature should it use?

  • AAvailability zones
  • BA region pair
  • CA resource lock
  • DA management group
Show the answer

Answer: A. Availability zones are separate locations inside a region and protect against a datacenter failure. A region pair protects against loss of a whole region.

S2An agency needs a version of Azure that is isolated for US government workloads. What is it?

  • ARegion pair
  • BAzure Government (a sovereign region)
  • CAvailability set
  • DGeography
Show the answer

Answer: B. Azure Government is a sovereign region built for US government needs.

S3What is true about the two regions of a region pair?

  • AThey are always on different continents and in different geographies
  • BThey share one datacenter building to reduce cost
  • CThey must be in the same availability zone so data stays close
  • DThey are in the same geography, and Azure staggers planned updates across them
Show the answer

Answer: D. Pairs sit in the same geography, usually far apart, and Azure staggers planned updates.

S4Which is a reason to pick a particular Azure region?

  • AThe color and size of the datacenter building
  • BCloseness to users, data residency, service availability and price
  • CThe number of subscriptions and resource groups you own
  • DThe names you gave to your resource groups and tags
Show the answer

Answer: B. Latency, compliance, available services and price differ by region.

S5What does a zone-redundant service do?

  • ARuns only in the one zone that you pick when you create it
  • BIs replicated across zones automatically by Azure
  • CRuns only on-premises and never replicates anywhere
  • DWorks only in sovereign regions such as Azure Government
Show the answer

Answer: B. Zone-redundant services spread their data or instances across zones for you. Zonal services run in one zone you choose.

S6How many availability zones does a region that supports them have at least?

  • AOne
  • BTwo
  • CThree
  • DTen
Show the answer

Answer: C. Regions that support availability zones have at least three.

7.2 Recall questions

R1What is an Azure region?

Show the answer

A set of datacenters in a latency-defined perimeter, connected by a low-latency network.

R2What does an availability zone have that makes it independent?

Show the answer

Its own power, cooling and networking.

R3Zones protect inside a region; what protects across regions?

Show the answer

Region pairs (and geo-redundancy).

R4Name the two sovereign regions.

Show the answer

Azure Government (US) and Azure China (operated by 21Vianet).

R5What is a geography?

Show the answer

A market area, such as a country or group of countries, that keeps data residency and compliance boundaries.

R6Who maintains the physical datacenters?

Show the answer

Microsoft.

8Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Region where you deploy; choose by latency, compliance, services, price
Region pair same geography, usually hundreds of miles apart; staggered updates; recovery priority
Sovereign regions Azure Government and Azure China: isolated instances for legal needs
Availability zone separate location in a region with its own power, cooling, network; at least three
Zonal vs zone-redundant you pick the zone vs Azure replicates across zones
Protection zones = datacenter failure; region pair = regional disaster
